audit_findings.title: The cash add-back may include operating cash that is not distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to $255.451 million of bridge cash is exposed; $50.1 million of non-distributable cash would erase the bear scenario's equity-value premium over the $11.88 market price
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge adds all cash and short-term investments to equity value even though field, settlement, restricted, or minimum operating cash must remain in the business
audit_findings.evidence: Cash and cash equivalents include bank deposit accounts; term bank deposit accounts; cash in the Company’s gaming terminals, ATMs, redemption terminals, and Company vaults.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the balance includes cash in terminals, ATMs, redemption terminals, and vaults, but it does not quantify the required operating portion. This is an unresolved classification issue, not a demonstrated $255.451 million error. It is material because only about one-fifth of the add-back would eliminate the bear-case premium.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the June 30, 2026 cash balance by bank cash, field cash, restricted or regulated funds, settlement float, and minimum operating liquidity; rerun every scenario using only distributable excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Recurring contract-acquisition spending may be absent from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.858 million of 2025 route and customer acquisition cash outflow, equal to 16.2% of the $73.3 million OE anchor; valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If related amortization is added back to earnings without deducting maintenance-level contract payments and commissions, anchor OE is overstated
audit_findings.evidence: The Company’s route and customer acquisition costs consist of fees paid, typically an upfront payment and future installment payment over the life of the contract, entered into with third parties and location partners.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates significant recurring cash investment in location contracts, but the supplied record does not show whether the OE calculation deducted it or how much represented maintenance rather than growth. An omission is therefore unresolved, but the filed spending is large relative to the anchor and reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2025 OE line by line; reconcile the $11.858 million cash outflow, payable movements, commissions, and $2.8 million route-cost amortization; classify maintenance versus growth spending and rerun with maintenance spending deducted.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition consideration liabilities may be missing from both OE and the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.743 million at June 30, 2026, or $0.22 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: Outstanding fixed and contingent acquisition consideration is a claim on equity and should enter either settlement cash flows or the equity bridge
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has a contingent consideration payable related to certain locations, as defined, in each respective acquisition agreement which are placed into operation during a specified period after the acquisition date.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates $4.249 million current and $15.494 million long-term consideration payable, while the supplied bridge contains no corresponding deduction. Deducting the full filed liability would reduce values to approximately $12.22, $13.96, and $16.00 per share for bear, base, and bull, respectively. That does not reverse any scenario's relationship to the $11.88 price and would lower the base-derived buy-below level by only about $0.15 per share.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the liability was not otherwise captured in OE, then deduct the June 2026 consideration payable in the bridge for completeness; no broader rerun is needed unless additional unrecorded obligations are identified.

audit_findings.title: Redeemable NCI creates a claim and possible ownership-basis mismatch
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.084 million carrying value at June 30, 2026, or $0.05 per diluted share; redemption value and any ownership-basis overstatement are unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated OE and cash may include 100% of Toucan while public shareholders own 85%, and the put creates a potential bridge claim
audit_findings.evidence: The noncontrolling interest holder may exercise its put option after seven years , or the occurrence of a change in control event at the Company.
audit_findings.explanation: The recorded carrying amount alone is not material relative to the $1.127-$1.471 billion scenario equity values. However, the filing says the put price is based on Toucan's Total Equity Value, not the $4.084 million carrying amount, and the supplied record does not establish whether OE and cash were reduced to the parent's 85% interest. Materiality therefore cannot be determined.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a parent-only Toucan reconciliation for net income, D&A, capex, working capital, and cash; calculate the put value under the contractual Total Equity Value formula and rerun with the appropriate minority allocation and redemption claim.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may capitalize income from an expired interest-rate hedge
audit_findings.magnitude: $6.9 million of 2025 pre-tax caplet income, equal to 9.4% of the $73.3 million OE anchor before tax normalization; valuation impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Nonrecurring hedge income lowers interest expense embedded in equity-level OE and is then capitalized through the forecast and terminal value
audit_findings.evidence: The Company also recognized interest income on the caplets of $ 6.9 million, $ 9.8 million, and $ 9.2 million for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 , and 2023 respectively, which is reflected in interest expense, net in the consolidated statements of operations and other comprehensive income.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that the $6.9 million benefit entered 2025 interest expense and that the caplets expired in January 2026. It is unresolved whether the OE calculation removed that benefit. The replacement collar and lower 2026 rates mean the proper adjustment is not necessarily the full $6.9 million, but the amount is large enough relative to the anchor to be material if perpetuated.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $6.9 million through the 2025 OE calculation and rerun using normalized interest based on the June 2026 debt balance, scheduled amortization, applicable credit margin, SOFR assumptions, and the collar's floor and cap.

audit_findings.title: FY2025 is not a normalized operating year for the new casino-and-racing business
audit_findings.magnitude: 2025 casino-and-racing revenue of $35.8 million and adjusted EBITDA of negative $0.002 million; first-half 2026 revenue of $24.0 million and adjusted EBITDA of $0.726 million; OE impact unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: A partial operating year can distort consolidated anchor OE, maintenance capital, and the single growth assumption applied to businesses with different economics
audit_findings.evidence: In April 2025, the casino opened and the racing season began at Fairmount.
audit_findings.explanation: The partial-year condition is demonstrated, but the filed segment adjusted EBITDA was approximately zero in 2025 and remains small in first-half 2026. That limits the demonstrated earnings effect, while segment-specific depreciation, maintenance capex, working capital, start-up costs, and normalized racing season economics are unavailable. Full-operation normalization could raise earnings or reveal additional capital requirements, so direction and materiality remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Build separate 2025 and first-half 2026 owner-earnings schedules for Fairmount, including start-up items and segment-specific maintenance capital; annualize only seasonally comparable operations and rerun distributed gaming and casino-and-racing with separate growth assumptions.
